methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $70M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Neustark, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Valentin Gutknecht and Johannes Tiefenthaler, has raised $70M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of 9 private frontier-tech peers (KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, and Enovix among them) and 1 public comparable (Linamar, ticker LNZA), all operating in the Climate & Energy sector at similar or adjacent stages.

Two valuation methods were triangulated. Stage-progression, anchoring to $70M total raised as a proxy and applying a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies $133M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M) yields a median of $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B. The stage-progression method reflects a more conservative read grounded in capital deployed; the peer-median captures observable market pricing for later-stage frontier-energy companies.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $113M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $566M. Key uncertainties include the timing and structure of Neustark's next funding round, the comparability of peer company technologies and market traction, and near-term shifts in climate-tech investor appetite.
